# AISE / Magnolia

> Multi-tenant service for software supply-chain observability and transparency:
> a signed, append-only Merkle transparency log of SBOMs, enriched with
> vulnerability, malicious-package, reputation, freshness and license signals,
> plus an LLM-assisted **CVE reachability evidence** analyser (`reach/`).
> Rust (axum + sqlx/Postgres) backend, React/TypeScript frontend. University
> course project (AISE module); EU CRA compliance is one application, not the
> whole purpose.

This file is an orientation map for LLM agents. It was written by reading the
code on 2026-09-17; where the prose docs disagree with the code, this file
follows the code and says so (see "Doc trust levels"). Hard rules for agents
live in `CLAUDE.md`. Read that first; it overrides anything here.

## Names

- **AISE**: the repo and course project. **Magnolia**: the product name used in
  the README, UI, crate names (`magnolia-*`) and binary (`magnolia-server`).
  They mean the same system.
- **reach**: the separate CVE-reachability analyser service in `reach/`.
- API keys look like `mag_<43 base64url chars>`; the upload config file is `Magnoliafile`.

## Hard rules you must not break (summary of CLAUDE.md)

1. All LLM calls go through an OpenAI-compatible `POST {base_url}/v1/chat/completions`.
   Endpoint, model, key and inference settings come only from env vars. The
   submission target is a local 4–8B model (Ollama / llama.cpp).
2. The AI gives **evidence, never a verdict.** "Symbol X is referenced at path:line"
   is fine. "This CVE is not exploitable" is out of scope, including in UI copy.
3. Confidence and priority values are **labels, not probabilities**.
4. Four failure modes are graded: server unavailable, timeout, invalid model
   output (validate, retry once, degrade), and processing failure. An inference
   failure must never break a non-AI flow.
5. Follow existing patterns: tenant toggle, sync loop, pure check in core.
   Migrations are append-only. Commit messages must be meaningful.
6. Never put secrets in the repo. Ask before destructive operations.

## Repository map

```
Cargo.toml            root workspace: crates/* only (reach is excluded on purpose)
crates/
  api/                axum HTTP server + background loops (binary: magnolia-server)
  core/               pure domain logic, no I/O: Merkle MMR, DSSE, compliance profiles,
                      license policy, purl, freshness, VEX import, schema validation
  auth/               API keys (SHA-256 hashed, constant-time), RBAC engine
                      examples/bootstrap_key.rs, keygen.rs
  signer/             Signer trait + LocalFileSigner (Ed25519)
  storage/            ObjectStore trait + FileStore + InMemoryStore (no S3 impl yet)
  db/                 ALL Postgres queries (lib.rs, ~2.8k lines) + models.rs
  audit/              audit log types
  dtrack/             Dependency-Track REST client
  osv/                OSV REST client (malicious-package advisories)
  depsdev/            deps.dev REST client (OpenSSF Scorecard reputation, freshness)
  reachability/       thin typed REST client for reach (create/get analysis, health)
migrations/           Postgres schema, YYYYMMDD00000N_name.sql, applied on server startup
frontend/src/         React UI. App.tsx is one ~7k-line file; api.ts is the typed client
reach/                SEPARATE Cargo project: CVE reachability analyser (own lockfile,
                      own [workspace], own SQLite DB, own Dockerfile)
  src/ai/             OpenAI-compatible ChatClient, prompts, startup probe
  src/pipeline/       stages A–E + baseline.rs (non-AI heuristic baseline)
  src/fetcher/        git fetch (hardened) + local + checkout cache
  src/lexer.rs        language-agnostic identifier scanner
  src/treesitter.rs   structural refinement (Rust, JS, Python, Go grammars)
  src/bin/eval.rs     eval harness
  eval/cases/         12 JSON eval cases; eval/fixtures/ plain dirs; eval/results/ (gitignored)
  scripts/reach-check.py  one-shot CLI (its default "verdict" mode is NOT submission-compliant)
scripts/              magnolia-upload.py/.sh (CI upload/verify CLI), bootstrap-dtrack.sh
tests/test_real_sboms.py  automated tests over real SBOMs in test-sboms/
docs/AI_DEVLOG.md     graded AI development log (append an episode after major agent work)
docker-compose.yml    db, api, frontend (profile), reach, ollama (profile), dtrack (profile)
docker-compose.dtrack.yml  full Dependency-Track stack + automatic bootstrap
```

## Runtime architecture

```
 browser ──▶ frontend (nginx :4000, profile "frontend") ──/api──▶ api (magnolia-server :3000)
                                                                   │  Postgres (db)
 CI ──▶ magnolia-upload.py ──────────────────────────────────────▶│  signing key / SBOM files (volume)
                                                                   │
                  background loops in api ─────────────────────────┤──▶ Dependency-Track (optional)
                  (dtrack, malicious, reputation, freshness,       │──▶ OSV, deps.dev
                   webhook delivery)                               │──▶ tenant webhooks
                                                                   │
                                   crates/reachability ────────────┴──▶ reach (:3100, SQLite)
                                                                          └──▶ OpenAI-compatible LLM
                                                                               (ollama profile or hosted)
```

- Only `api` publishes a host port by default. `db`, `dependency-track` and `reach` stay
  on the internal compose network.
- The api migrates its own schema on startup (`sqlx::migrate!`) and rebuilds each
  tenant's in-memory MMR from `merkle_leaves`.
- Optional integrations are **presence-gated** by env vars. If they are unset, the feature
  is off and the UI hides it: `DTRACK_URL`+`DTRACK_API_KEY`(`_FILE`),
  `AISE_REACH_BASE_URL`+`AISE_REACH_TOKEN`. They can also be killed with
  `DISABLE_MALICIOUS_PACKAGE_CHECK` or `DISABLE_REPUTATION_CHECK`.

## Core concepts (AISE side)

- **Tenant** = one domain. Each tenant has its own full data isolation and its own
  Merkle tree / signed-tree-head chain. Exactly one tenant is `is_platform` (the
  bootstrap tenant). It is admin-only and rejects SBOM uploads.
- **Namespace**: a hierarchical path like `/product/v1`. A key's `namespace_scope` is a
  segment-aware prefix match. Tenants can require namespaces to be registered before upload.
- **Roles**: `super_admin`, `domain_admin`, `uploader`, `auditor`.
  **Actions** (`crates/auth/src/rbac.rs`): Upload, Read, Annotate, ManageKeys, ManageAcls,
  ManageSettings, ManageTenants (platform-level), and ManageTenantData, a privileged tenant-data action
  that is withheld from domain_admin. Only a platform-tenant super_admin may pass
  `?tenant_id=` to act across tenants.
  The extractor is `AuthGrant` (`crates/api/src/auth.rs`).
- **Manifest**: signed metadata for one uploaded SBOM or document (namespace, version,
  hash chain via previous manifest, optional `source_commit`). It is signed as a
  **DSSE envelope** around an in-toto Statement whose subject digest is the SBOM hash.
  Revocation is a status flag, never a delete.
- **Signed Tree Head (STH)**: signed MMR root + size. Inclusion and consistency proofs are
  served by the API and verified client-side in the UI (`frontend/src/merkle.ts`).
- **Findings**: `dtrack_findings` (cached from Dependency-Track) plus
  `malicious_component_findings` (OSV). Analysts set a VEX status
  (`affected|not_affected|fixed|under_investigation`; `not_affected` needs a justification)
  and add comments. VEX export/import is per manifest.

### Upload path (`handlers::upload_sbom`)

1. Parse the multipart body (`sbom_file`, `format`, `namespace`, `version`, optional
   `source_commit`, which is rejected if malformed).
2. Run the RBAC/namespace-scope check, then `validate_sbom_content`.
3. Run `enforce_compliance` (tenant-enabled NTIA / BSI TR-03183 profiles) and
   `enforce_license_policy`.
4. Run the registered-namespace check and reject uploads to the platform tenant.
5. Store the bytes, append the MMR leaf, sign the STH, and insert it.
6. Build the in-toto Statement, sign it over the DSSE PAE and store the manifest.
7. Index components (`sbom_components`), then the later sync loops push and enrich.
   Webhooks and audit logs record the event.

`POST /api/v1/verify` runs the same policy checks as a dry run (no storage, no leaf). This
is the CI gate.

### Postgres tables (from migrations)

tenants, api_keys, audit_logs, signed_tree_heads, merkle_leaves, merkle_nodes, manifests,
namespace_current_hidden, registered_namespaces, sbom_components,
compliance_profile_settings, tenant_license_policies, dtrack_projects, dtrack_findings,
dtrack_push_failures, finding_comments, malicious_component_findings,
component_reputation, component_freshness, webhook_endpoints, webhook_deliveries,
namespace_repos, finding_reachability. Many per-tenant toggles are columns on `tenants`.

### Background loops (`crates/api/src/*_sync.rs`, spawned in `main.rs`)

- `dtrack_sync::run_sync_loop` pushes BOMs and pulls findings.
- `malicious_sync` runs OSV checks (via `malicious_check.rs`, which also fetches advisory
  text with `get_vuln`).
- `reputation_sync` pulls deps.dev / Scorecard data, bucketed in `reputation_bucket.rs`.
- `freshness_sync` checks freshness and EOL.
- `webhooks::run_webhook_delivery_loop` delivers webhooks.
- Shared cadence helper: `sync_loop::run_burst_loop`. Intervals come from
  `*_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECS` and `SYNC_BURST_INTERVAL_SECS`.
- Each signal has a tenant toggle, a `POST /api/v1/<signal>/sync` force endpoint and a
  `GET …/status` endpoint.

### REST API route groups (`crates/api/src/lib.rs::create_router`)

All routes use `Authorization: Bearer mag_…`. **There is no OpenAPI spec for this API yet.**

| Group | Routes |
|---|---|
| Meta | `/health`, `/install.sh`, `/install.py`, `/api/v1/whoami`, `/config`, `/signing-key` |
| Log & proofs | `POST /upload`, `POST /verify`, `/tree-head/latest`, `/tree-head/:size`, `/proof/inclusion/:i`, `/proof/consistency/:old/:new`, `/leaves`, `POST /snapshot` |
| Manifests | `/manifest/:hash`, `…/vex`, `POST …/vex/import`, `…/diff`, `POST …/revoke`, `/manifests/current`, `/namespaces/manifests` |
| Findings | `/findings`, `POST …/findings/:key/triage`, `…/findings/:key/comments`, `…/findings/:key/reachability` (GET status, POST request) |
| Search / blast radius | `/search/components`, `POST /search/reindex`, `/components/affected`, `/vulnerabilities/:id/affected` |
| Signals | `/dtrack/sync`, `/reputation/{sync,status,components}`, `/freshness/{sync,status}`, `/malicious/{sync,status}` |
| Settings (tenant toggles) | `/settings/{dtrack-sync,semver-version,reputation-sync,freshness,malicious-check,namespace-registration,license-policy,namespace-repos}`, `/compliance/{profiles,settings}` |
| Namespaces | `/namespaces/hidden`, `/namespaces/registered` |
| Admin | `/keys`, `/keys/:id/revoke`, `/tenants`, `DELETE /tenants/:id`, `POST /tenants/cache/clear`, `/audit-logs` |
| Webhooks | `/webhooks`, `/webhooks/:id` (PATCH/DELETE), `…/test`, `…/deliveries` |

(The `/api/v1` prefix is omitted after the first rows.) Handlers are in
`crates/api/src/handlers.rs` (~5.6k lines). Search it by handler name.

## The AI feature: `reach/` (CVE reachability evidence)

Question it answers: *given this advisory and this exact commit, where does the code
reference the symbols the advisory names?*

| Stage | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| A | deterministic | Package presence from manifests and lock files, plus an identifier index. Zero evidence short-circuits with **no LLM call**. |
| B | LLM | Advisory → ruleset (symbols, patterns, preconditions, optional `NestedCallPattern`). Schema-validated, one repair retry. **Grounding check:** a symbol not in the advisory text is dropped and counted. |
| C | deterministic | Ranked occurrence search (prod > tests > comments), capped, with snippets. Tree-sitter widens snippets to function boundaries. |
| D | LLM, per site | Ordinal label `likely_relevant / unclear / likely_irrelevant` plus a cited line. **Citation check:** the line must exist and lie inside the shown snippet. |
| E | pure fn | `rubric.rs` turns the fired rules into a priority label plus a trace. |

- Every stage degrades and records a StageOutcome. The only hard failure is being unable
  to fetch the requested source. An inference outage produces a deterministic-only
  report, never a 5xx.
- `src/ai/mod.rs`: `ChatClient::{complete, complete_json, probe}`, `AiError` (all four
  graded failure modes), `parse_lenient` / `extract_json_object`.
- **Startup probe is fatal.** `main.rs` *awaits* a real json-mode test completion before
  binding. On `unreachable`, `responded_with_error` or `responded_but_unusable`, the
  process exits 1. The result is exposed at `GET /health` → `ai_probe`.
- REST: `POST /api/v1/analyses` (`advisory_text`, `osv_id`, `package_name`, `ecosystem`,
  `repo_url`, `commit` as full 40/64-hex *or* `ref` — a branch/tag resolved once at request
  time via `src/fetcher/resolve.rs` and returned as `commit`), `GET /api/v1/analyses[/:id]`, `/health`,
  `/openapi.json` (utoipa), `/docs` (Swagger UI). Auth uses one static bearer token,
  `REACH_API_TOKEN`. If `repo_url` is omitted, only stage B runs. That is the declared
  fallback feature: grounded advisory extraction.
- Security: https/local-path allowlist (`GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL`), no leading `-`, no
  userinfo, token via `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `core.symlinks=false`, exact commits only, repo
  content never executed. Advisory text and code are fenced as data in prompts, with the
  fence markers scrubbed.
- Config (`src/config.rs`): `REACH_AI_{BASE_URL,MODEL,API_KEY,TIMEOUT_SECS,MAX_TOKENS,TEMPERATURE}`,
  `REACH_API_TOKEN`, `REACH_SERVER_ADDR`, `REACH_DB_PATH`, `REACH_CACHE_{DIR,MB}`,
  `REACH_MAX_{SITES,SCORED_SITES,REPO_MB,FILE_KB,ADVISORY_CHARS}`, `REACH_GIT_TOKEN`.
  Reasoning models (deepseek-r1) need `REACH_AI_MAX_TOKENS` of 6000 or more.
  `REACH_MAX_SCORED_SITES` is the main latency knob (one LLM call per site).
- Eval: `cd reach && cargo run --bin eval` (full), `-- --baseline-only` (no LLM server;
  also exercises degradation), `-- --case 06`. 12 cases cover nominal, package absent, no
  symbols, ambiguous, injection via advisory, injection via code comment, malformed,
  out of scope, advisory-only, lexical false positive, monorepo subpath and hallucination
  bait. Metrics: extraction P/R/F1 vs. the heuristic baseline, priority accuracy, citation
  pass rate, first-try structured-output rate, per-label precision, injection resistance
  and latency. Forbidden-text checks search only **model-authored** text
  (`model_authored_text()` in `src/bin/eval.rs`). Do not "simplify" that back into
  searching the whole report.

### AISE ↔ reach integration

- The migration `20260830000003_reachability.sql` adds these:
  - `namespace_repos`, which records where a namespace's *own* source lives. It is set
    explicitly and never inferred from SBOM component URLs.
  - `manifests.source_commit`, which the upload CLI sends only from a clean git tree.
  - `finding_reachability`, which links a finding to an analysis. It is append-only in
    practice.
- AISE resolves the repo, commit and advisory text (the `dtrack_findings` description),
  calls `ReachClient::create_analysis`, stores the id and proxies the report verbatim on
  read. If reach is unreachable, it shows status `unavailable`.
- Revision choice (`crates/api/src/reachability.rs::choose_revision`): the manifest's own
  `source_commit` wins; otherwise the namespace mapping's `revision` is sent as `ref`
  (`commit_source = namespace_revision`); with neither, the analysis is blocked.
- Background loop `run_reachability_auto_loop` queues analyses for untriaged findings on
  the current manifest of namespaces with `auto_analyze`, capped by
  `REACHABILITY_AUTO_MAX_IN_FLIGHT`, audited as `system:reachability-auto`, and keeps the
  `finding_reachability.status/priority` cache fresh for list badges.
- UI: `ReachabilityPanel` (button, provenance line, "review help": advisory summary, things
  to confirm, call sites linked to the forge at the analysed commit, false matches collapsed,
  "How was this determined?" trace), `ReachabilityBadge` in the Findings list, and
  `SourceRepoSettings` (revision + automatic toggle) in `App.tsx`.

## Frontend

- CRA app. `App.tsx` holds nearly all components as top-level functions. The main ones are
  Dashboard, Upload, VerifyGateCheck, Leaves / NamespaceTree, SbomDetailPanel, Findings,
  FindingTriageControls, FindingComments, ReachabilityPanel, ComponentSearch, Proofs
  (InclusionCard / ConsistencyCard), Keys, Tenants / TenantSelector, Audit, Settings,
  WebhooksSettings and ConnectionGate. Small extracted components live in
  `src/components/`, and API key state lives in `src/context/ApiContext.tsx`.
- `api.ts` holds typed fetch wrappers for every endpoint. Add new endpoints there.
- The dev server runs on :4000 and proxies `/api` and `/health` to 127.0.0.1:3000.

## Commands

```sh
# AISE backend
cargo run --bin magnolia-server                 # needs DATABASE_URL; listens 127.0.0.1:3000
cargo run -p magnolia-auth --example bootstrap_key   # mint BOOTSTRAP_SUPER_ADMIN_KEY
cargo test --workspace                          # does NOT build reach/

# reach (always from inside reach/)
cd reach && cargo test && cargo clippy
cd reach && cargo run                           # :3100; exits 1 if the LLM probe fails

# frontend
cd frontend && npm start
cd frontend && npx tsc --noEmit && CI=true npx react-scripts build   # eslint warnings fail CI builds

# full stack
docker compose up --build
docker compose --profile ollama up -d ollama && docker compose exec ollama ollama pull gemma3:4b
docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.dtrack.yml up -d

# upload / CI gate
MAGNOLIA_API_KEY=mag_… scripts/magnolia-upload.py            # reads ./Magnoliafile
MAGNOLIA_API_KEY=mag_… scripts/magnolia-upload.py verify
```

Before calling work done, run `cargo test --workspace`, then `tsc`, then the `CI=true`
build. If `reach/` changed, also run `cd reach && cargo test`.

## Key env vars (api)

`DATABASE_URL`, `SERVER_ADDR`, `SIGNING_KEY_PATH`, and `STORAGE_PATH`. If `STORAGE_PATH`
is unset, SBOM bytes are kept in memory and lost on restart. Also:

- `BOOTSTRAP_SUPER_ADMIN_KEY`, `BOOTSTRAP_TENANT_DOMAIN`, `BOOTSTRAP_TENANT_NAME`
- `DEV_MODE`, which relaxes one RBAC check. Never enable it in prod.
- `DTRACK_URL`, `DTRACK_API_KEY`, `DTRACK_API_KEY_FILE`
- `*_SYNC_INTERVAL_SECS`, `WEBHOOK_DELIVERY_INTERVAL_SECS`, `SYNC_BURST_INTERVAL_SECS`
- `REACHABILITY_AUTO_INTERVAL_SECS`, `REACHABILITY_AUTO_MAX_IN_FLIGHT`, `DISABLE_REACHABILITY_AUTO`
- `DISABLE_MALICIOUS_PACKAGE_CHECK`, `DISABLE_REPUTATION_CHECK`
- `AISE_REACH_BASE_URL`, `AISE_REACH_TOKEN`

`.env.example` covers the compose deployment.

## Gotchas

- `reach/` is not a workspace member. Root `cargo test --workspace` never compiles it.
- sqlx queries are **runtime-checked**. SQL errors only show up when the query runs, so
  smoke-test new queries against a live DB. All queries belong in `crates/db/src/lib.rs`.
- New per-tenant settings follow the pattern: migration → `set_tenant_*` in db → GET/POST
  `/settings/…` → frontend switch.
- New pure policy or compliance logic goes in `crates/core` with unit tests and no I/O
  (see the `ComplianceProfile` trait in `compliance.rs`).
- `/verify` and upload share their policy checks. Change them together.
- Reachability refuses to run without `source_commit` and a `namespace_repos` mapping, by
  design. Don't add a fallback to a branch head.
- reach error paths must not echo raw panic payloads or repo contents. `worker.rs` runs
  each job in its own task as a panic boundary.
- In `lexer.rs`, use `str::get` or the `starts_with_at` helper, never `text[i..]` at byte
  offsets. Multi-byte UTF-8 in source files caused a real panic there.
- CLAUDE.md names the AI env vars `AISE_AI_*`, but the code uses **`REACH_AI_*`**, because
  all LLM work lives in reach. There is no `crates/ai`.

## Doc trust levels

- **Current:** `CLAUDE.md`, `reach/README.md`, `reach/eval/README.md`, `.env.example`,
  `docs/AI_DEVLOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md` (see its "Status log" section), `ARCHITECTURE.md`
  (rewritten against the code on 2026-09-17), and the reach sections of `README.md`.
- **Partly stale:** the rest of `README.md`. Its endpoint table lists only the original
  subset of routes, and its "Design Philosophy" section still describes S3/WORM as if
  implemented.
- **Historical planning notes** (useful for intent only, not truth): `Features.md`,
  `tech.md`, `DTRACK_PLAN.md`, `SUPPLY_CHAIN_SIGNALS_PLAN.md`, `SUPPLY_CHAIN_TODO.md`,
  `VEX_TODO.md`, `IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md`.

## Known gaps (course deliverables still open, as of 2026-09-17)

- No OpenAPI document for the AISE API. Only reach has one.
- No CI: `.github/workflows` is absent.
- The full real-model eval run is incomplete. Rerun it against a Gemma-class local model,
  and force-add a results file, since `eval/results/` is gitignored.
- The reachability UI has not been visually verified.
- Production items are not done: S3/Object Lock storage, KMS signer, Postgres RLS, rate
  limiting, TLS termination (left to a reverse proxy).
